Yanuni

Directed by Richard Ladkani; producers Juma Xipaia, Leonardo DiCaprio, Anita Ladkani, Richard Ladkani, Jennifer Davisson and Phillip Watson.

Whose Story: Centers Juma Xipaia of the Xipaya people in Brazil, who is credited as both participant and producer. Instituto Juma identifies her as its founder. This film does not represent every Amazonian Indigenous community.

Full Film

Before Watching: Discusses threats against Indigenous defenders, illegal mining and dangerous environmental enforcement operations.

    Full Film

    Yanuni

    Full Film · 113m 42s · YouTube Edition · 2025

    Directed by Richard Ladkani; producers Juma Xipaia, Leonardo DiCaprio, Anita Ladkani, Richard Ladkani, Jennifer Davisson and Phillip Watson.

    Malaika Pictures / Leonardo DiCaprio official channel

    Details And Official Source

    Juma Xipaia defends her people's Amazonian land while navigating leadership and motherhood. Family resilience meets threats from illegal mining and the struggle for Indigenous sovereignty.

    Whose Story: Centers Juma Xipaia of the Xipaya people in Brazil, who is credited as both participant and producer. Instituto Juma identifies her as its founder. This film does not represent every Amazonian Indigenous community.

    Full film on producer Leonardo DiCaprio's official YouTube channel. Location, account or provider restrictions may apply.

    Before Watching: Discusses threats against Indigenous defenders, illegal mining and dangerous environmental enforcement operations.

    Language And Translation
    Translate The Whole Page

    Use your browser's Translate Page option. On a phone, look in the browser menu. On desktop Chrome, right-click the page and choose Translate. Available languages depend on your browser.

    Video audio and captions are separate. Use each video's own caption controls when available; ZOTHEOS does not translate the recording.

    Translate A Reading Section

    Choose the selected story, the Theater introduction or the curation notes, then choose your language in Google Translate.

    Choose Language In Google Translate ↗

    This opens Google and sends only the selected public reading text when you press the link. Searches and form entries are excluded. Automatic translations may change names or meaning. Check the original sources. Without page scripts, copy a passage into Google Translate yourself.

    How Titles Are Selected

    Attention With Responsibility.

    Distinct stories, official sources and honest viewing notes. No film stands for every Nation.

    Read The Selection Method And Historical Context

    Selection uses official filmmaker, publisher and community sources. Credits, source-check dates and viewing limits remain with each story. Inclusion is not an endorsement by a Nation, independent verification of every statement or a claim that the full recording was watched for this collection.

    Trailers, excerpts and recorded presentations are labeled. Official viewing pages may require payment, an account or access from a particular country. Availability can change. Videos remain with their authorized providers; ZOTHEOS does not copy or host them.

    History In Context

    The collection includes the official Daughter of a Lost Bird excerpt on Indigenous adoption. Its child-removal percentage is historical testimony about research before the Indian Child Welfare Act, not a present-day removal rate. Read NICWA’s Historical Context.

    This growing collection is incomplete. Corrections, living cultures, community-led restoration and careful source review guide its growth.

    Theater Privacy

    Fonts and page code load from this site. Theme, motion and effect intensity preferences stay in your browser. The Theater does not save searches or film selections. A story link carries its record ID in the URL fragment; choosing other stories does not rewrite your URL or search history.

    Official thumbnails load automatically from their listed image providers. The selected YouTube, PBS, Vimeo or National Film Board player also loads automatically, ready for its Play control. These providers receive your IP address and request information when contacted; their own privacy policies apply. Eligible YouTube and Vimeo previews may start without sound when at least 60% of the screen and controls are visible, except in Still or when the device asks for reduced motion. They pause outside view or when the tab is hidden. Your Pause holds until Play. Playback uses data and sends playback reports to the provider. Previews stop after 45 seconds on desktop and 15 seconds on phones unless you deliberately take control. Sound starts only when you choose it.

    YouTube uses its privacy-enhanced player domain and Vimeo requests its do-not-track mode. Neither makes playback anonymous or guarantees that a provider collects no data. Selecting another story replaces the current player and contacts that provider. This page sends play, pause, sound and caption commands to YouTube and Vimeo through their player interfaces. Caption availability is checked by the player; dated metadata is a starting point and can change. Use native National Film Board and PBS controls. Other provider controls remain available.

    Source links contact their destinations when followed. Publishers can restrict or remove a title. If playback fails, use the official source. Report A Correction.
